name: Model
simple: A Model is a container that groups parts together into one thing, like a car, a house, or a character. You can move, size and copy the whole group at once instead of part by part. Every player's character is a Model too.
analogy: A Model is like a LEGO set glued into one build. It's still made of many bricks, but you can pick up the whole spaceship and move it in one go.
whenToUse: Group the parts of one object (a tree, a car, an NPC) so they move and copy together.
Move a whole object somewhere with PivotTo or MoveTo.
Make an object bigger or smaller with ScaleTo.
Find out how big an object is (GetExtentsSize, GetBoundingBox).
where: Usually in Workspace (so it shows up in the world) or in ServerStorage / ReplicatedStorage (as a template to clone). Make one in Studio by selecting parts and pressing Ctrl+G (Cmd+G on Mac), or with `Instance.new("Model")`. Use a Folder instead if your group isn't a 3D object (for example, a bunch of scripts).

terms.part: A single 3D block, ball, or mesh in the world. Models are made of parts.
terms.PrimaryPart: The one part of a Model that acts as its main handle. The Model's pivot follows it when things move.
terms.pivot: The point a Model moves and spins around. Moving the pivot moves the whole Model.
terms.CFrame: A value that stores a position AND a rotation together, like 'stand here, facing that way'.
terms.Vector3: Three numbers (X, Y, Z) for a position, size or movement in 3D. Y is up.
terms.bounding box: The smallest invisible box that fits around everything in the Model.
terms.world space: Measuring from the map's own X, Y, Z directions, not from the Model's own facing.
terms.scale factor: A size multiplier. 1 is original size, 2 is double, 0.5 is half.
terms.streaming: A game setting where players' devices only load the parts of the world near them. Far-away Models may not exist on their device yet.
terms.clone: Make an exact copy of an object with :Clone().

examples.title: Clone a model and place it
examples.place: Script in ServerScriptService (put a Model named Tree in ServerStorage)
examples.code:
local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
local treeTemplate = ServerStorage:WaitForChild("Tree")

for i = 1, 5 do
    local tree = treeTemplate:Clone()
    -- PivotTo moves the whole model; place trees 10 studs apart along X
    tree:PivotTo(CFrame.new(i * 10, 0, 0))
    tree.Parent = workspace
end
explain: Clone makes a copy of the whole Model, with every part inside.
PivotTo moves the Model so its pivot ends up at the CFrame you give. CFrame.new(10, 0, 0) is the spot X=10, Y=0, Z=0.
Setting Parent to workspace makes them show up in the world.

examples.title: Grow a model and lift it
examples.place: Script inside a Model in Workspace
examples.code:
local model = script.Parent

print("Size before: " .. tostring(model:GetExtentsSize()))
model:ScaleTo(2) -- twice as big as its original size
print("Size after: " .. tostring(model:GetExtentsSize()))

-- Move it 10 studs straight up, keeping its rotation
model:TranslateBy(Vector3.new(0, 10, 0))
explain: GetExtentsSize tells you how big the Model is, as a Vector3 (width, height, depth).
ScaleTo(2) makes everything twice the ORIGINAL size. Calling ScaleTo(2) again doesn't make it 4 times; it stays 2.
TranslateBy shifts the Model by an amount. If it was at (0, 5, 0), it ends up at (0, 15, 0).

gotchas: Set a PrimaryPart (or the pivot) for models that move, so they move predictably.
Use PivotTo to move a Model. The old SetPrimaryPartCFrame is deprecated.
MoveTo pops the model upward if something is in the way and doesn't keep its rotation. Use PivotTo for exact placement.
Parts inside a Model that aren't welded or anchored will fall apart when the game runs.
With streaming on, a LocalScript might see the Model before all its parts arrive. Use WaitForChild, or set ModelStreamingMode to Atomic.

Model.LevelOfDetail.simple: For games with streaming on: what to show when the Model is far away and not loaded. StreamingMesh or SLIM show a simpler, lower-detail copy so far things don't just vanish. Disabled or Automatic show nothing extra.

Model.ModelStreamingMode.simple: For games with streaming on: controls how this Model is loaded on players' devices. For example Atomic means all of it loads together, and Persistent means it stays loaded. Change it in Studio or in a server Script, never in a LocalScript.
Model.ModelStreamingMode.example: model.ModelStreamingMode = Enum.ModelStreamingMode.Atomic -- load all parts together

Model.PrimaryPart.simple: The part inside the Model that acts as its main handle. When physics moves the Model, its pivot follows this part. Not set by default. It must be a part inside this Model.

Model.Scale.simple: Studio-only box in the Properties window to resize the Model. Scripts can't use it; call ScaleTo and GetScale instead.

Model.WorldPivot.simple: Where the Model's pivot is, as a CFrame, when it has no PrimaryPart. If the Model has a PrimaryPart, the PrimaryPart's pivot is used instead and this is ignored.

Model:AddPersistentPlayer.simple: For streaming games: keeps this Model always loaded for one player, even when they're far away. ModelStreamingMode must be PersistentPerPlayer.

Model:BreakJoints.simple: Old — use WeldConstraints and destroy them yourself instead.

Model:breakJoints.simple: Old — use WeldConstraints and destroy them yourself instead.

Model:GetBoundingBox.simple: Gives two things: a CFrame for the center of the invisible box around the Model, and a Vector3 for that box's size.
Model:GetBoundingBox.example:
local center, size = model:GetBoundingBox()
print("Center:", center.Position, "Size:", size)

Model:GetExtentsSize.simple: Gives the size of the smallest box that fits around all the parts, as a Vector3 (width, height, depth) in studs.
Model:GetExtentsSize.example:
local size = model:GetExtentsSize()
print("This model is " .. size.Y .. " studs tall")

Model:GetPersistentPlayers.simple: From a server Script: gives the list of players this Model is kept loaded for. From a LocalScript it only checks the local player.
Model:GetPersistentPlayers.example:
for _, player in model:GetPersistentPlayers() do
    print(player.Name)
end

Model:GetScale.simple: Tells you the Model's current scale factor. A new Model starts at 1; ScaleTo changes it.
Model:GetScale.example: print(model:GetScale()) -- 1 for a model that was never resized

Model:MoveTo.simple: Moves the Model so its PrimaryPart is at a position. If something is in the way, the Model is pushed upward until it fits. It does not keep the Model's rotation.
Model:MoveTo.gotcha: Use PivotTo when you need an exact spot or want to keep the rotation.

Model:RemovePersistentPlayer.simple: Stops keeping this Model loaded for a player (undoes AddPersistentPlayer). It may stay loaded while they are close.

Model:ScaleTo.simple: Resizes the whole Model (parts, joints, effects, sounds' distances) to a scale factor compared to its ORIGINAL size, around its pivot. ScaleTo(2) is double size, ScaleTo(1) goes back exactly to normal.
Model:ScaleTo.example:
model:ScaleTo(0.5) -- half size
task.wait(2)
model:ScaleTo(1)   -- back to normal

Model:TranslateBy.simple: Shifts the Model by an amount in world space, keeping its rotation. A Model at (0, 5, 0) moved by (2, 0, 0) ends up at (2, 5, 0). It can overlap other things.
